newsitem.title: USA: U.S., North Korea hold bilateral talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., North Korea hold bilateral talks.

text.p: The United States and North Korea discussed bilateral issues in New York on Tuesday despite an impasse over proposed peace talks with South Korea, the State Department said.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Washington was committed to a bilateral dialogue with Pyongyang despite its failure so far unconditionally to accept the proposal for peace talks that would also involve South Korea and China.

Burns said the United States continued to oppose Pyongyang's demand for more food aid before agreeing to join the peace talks. He said those differences "apparently will not be closed quickly" and the future of the peace proposal was in Pyongyang's hands.
South Korean negotiators flew home to Seoul Tuesday after talks in New York failed to produce a clear-cut acceptance by Pyongyang of the four-party peace proposal.
The U.S. negotiators headed for Washington after holding a meeting with the North Korean side on Tuesday, a U.S. official said.

The meeting dealt with bilateral issues such as U.S. servicemen still missing from the 1950-53 Korean War, North Korean missile exports and establishing liaison offices in Washington and Pyongyang, the official added.
